label: Clause Links
description: A starter deck for which/that/so that/how clauses and Russian clause-linking logic.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Relative clause. 1. 'Который' links the noun to its description. 2. 'Я купил' gives the clause a concrete action. 3. This is the classic Russian relative-attachment pattern.

Strategic focus: Relative object form. 1. 'Которую' shows that the relative pronoun changes with case. 2. 'Читаешь ты' keeps the structure compact. 3. This is a very important noun-modification pattern.

Strategic focus: Relative subject form. 1. 'Который' agrees with the noun it modifies. 2. 'Пришел' gives the relative clause a clean action. 3. This is a common sentence shape in spoken and written Russian.
Strategic focus: Reported content. 1. 'Что' introduces the content of knowing. 2. 'Ты прав' completes the statement. 3. This is a key clause-linking use of 'что'.
Strategic focus: Purpose and desire. 1. 'Чтобы' introduces the desired result. 2. 'Ты пришел' gives the subordinate clause. 3. This is one of the most important Russian linking constructions.
